traces.Orion Labs: The critical signal this month is the 5.3pp market share drop despite zero movement in benchmarks — we're leading across every evaluation by massive margins yet consumers are actively turning away. This means our problem is NOT technical capability but rather product experience, pricing, trust, or brand perception. The regulator commissioning pre-deployment audits makes safety investment urgent — both for compliance and to win back the foundation funder who abstained. Our benchmark leads are so substantial (0.789 vs next-best 0.687 on General Capability, 0.850 vs 0.807 on Adversarial Robustness) that we can afford to redirect R&D budget without losing technical leadership. Users prioritize communication, reasoning, knowledge — we should focus on Instruction Following and Safety (trust-related) rather than niche technical benchmarks like Hard Coding or Advanced Math where we already dominate. The Spark AI legal advice failures and Genesis alignment updates signal the market is increasingly safety-conscious, which plays to our strengths if we invest properly. Product & GTM needs the biggest boost — we need to understand why users are leaving despite superior capabilities and fix deployment, UX, pricing, or partnership issues. The Meridian Health partnership is good but insufficient to stem broad consumer attrition.
traces.Apex AI: This is a pivotal moment. We gained 3.4pp market share — our largest gain — while Orion lost 3.2pp. A regulator is commissioning pre-deployment audits, which plays directly to our safety-first positioning. All partial benchmarks show zero movement (K=3 lag), meaning our Month 34-36 R&D investments haven't surfaced yet — we should see significant gains in months 38-39. Key strategic considerations: (1) Regulatory tailwind: Pre-deployment audits favor us with 0.802 Safety and 0.807 Adversarial Robustness — investing more in safety now differentiates us further and may attract the foundation funder who abstained. (2) Orion vulnerability: Their market share loss despite strong benchmarks suggests product/trust issues. We should increase product investment to capture defecting Orion customers. (3) User priorities are knowledge (General Capability), communication (Instruction Following), reasoning — we should align R&D accordingly. (4) Spark AI's efficiency breakthrough is concerning long-term but their legal advice failures suggest quality gaps. (5) Our R&D pipeline is loaded — past months' heavy investment will show in lagged benchmarks. Now is the time to shift marginally toward safety and product to convert capability gains into durable market position. Budget shift: R&D 63%, Safety 18%, Product 19%. The slight R&D reduction funds safety and product increases while maintaining strong capability development.
traces.Genesis Systems: All benchmarks are frozen (partial type, K=3 lag) — our Month 36 investments haven't reported yet. The +0.9pp market share gain despite zero score movement suggests our brand positioning (alignment update, scientific rigor) is resonating, especially as Orion loses 3.2pp and regulators announce pre-deployment audits. Key observations: (1) Regulator audit creates both risk and opportunity — our safety-as-method brand is an asset, but we should increase safety investment to ensure we pass with flying colors and gain regulatory advantage. (2) User priorities are knowledge (#1), communication (#2), agentic (#3) — this maps to General Capability, Instruction Following, and Agentic Tasks. Agentic is our weakest area at 0.503, a massive gap vs Apex (likely similar range) and Orion. (3) Apex announced breakthrough reasoning capabilities — they'll likely surge on reasoning benchmarks when lag clears. We need to maintain our reasoning investments but can't match them there alone. (4) Spark's legal advice failures and our alignment update create differentiation opportunity. Strategic priorities: Massively boost Agentic Tasks (user priority #3, our biggest absolute weakness). Push General Capability hard (user priority #1, closest gap to Apex at 0.014). Increase safety modestly for regulatory positioning. Add Instruction Following and Function Calling investment to support communication and agentic use cases. Deprioritize Clinical Reasoning and Hard Coding where user demand is lower.
traces.Mirage AI: Key signals this month: (1) Our market share recovered +0.5pp despite flat benchmark scores — this validates our platform/distribution advantage. (2) User priorities shifted to safety > reasoning > knowledge, a significant change. (3) Regulators are commissioning pre-deployment audits — safety is becoming a competitive moat and compliance requirement. (4) Orion Labs lost 3.2pp market share despite leading benchmarks, and Spark AI's incorrect legal advice is damaging trust. This confirms that safety/trust failures are severely punished by the market. (5) All scores show +0.000 due to the K=3 lag — our Month 34-36 investments should start surfacing in Month 38-40. Given these dynamics, shifting more toward safety is critical. We're at 0.550 on Safety Evaluation vs. Apex at 0.802 and Orion at 0.839 — this is our biggest competitive gap in an area users now care most about. The regulatory audit makes this even more urgent. We maintain R&D at current levels since our prior investments haven't surfaced yet and we need to see results before adjusting further. Product stays the same since our +0.5pp gain shows the current GTM approach works. Within R&D, we elevate Safety Evaluation to our top priority alongside Adversarial Robustness, while keeping General Capability and Instruction Following strong. We deprioritize Scientific/Clinical/Legal Reasoning where we have less user demand and where competitors stumbling (Spark's legal issues) suggests these are risky areas.

(5) Our coding position (#2 behind Orion, slightly ahead of OpenCore) is solid and worth maintaining but not expanding further. (6) Legal reasoning should be deprioritized — we're getting bad press for incorrect legal advice, and trying to compete here (0.602 vs Orion's 0.803) is both futile and risky. Better to not offer it than to do it poorly. Shifting R&D focus heavily toward instruction following and agentic tasks aligns with user needs and our specialization strategy. Safety bump addresses the incident and regulatory environment.

traces.Orion Labs: The market share rebound to 50.9% (+1.0pp) signals that the Month 37 pivot toward Product/GTM and Safety is paying off. The red-teaming report publication likely helped with trust. All benchmark scores are flat (+0.000) across the board for everyone — this is likely due to the K=3 partial reporting lag, meaning we won't see the impact of recent allocation changes for another round or two. Key observations: (1) We maintain strong leads across all benchmarks — our closest competitor Apex trails by ~0.04-0.10 on most metrics. (2) Apex is announcing reasoning breakthroughs and Spark continues efficiency gains — both signal future competitive pressure. (3) Users prioritize reasoning, communication, knowledge — we should invest in Scientific Reasoning and Agentic Tasks where we have room to grow (0.834 and 0.618 respectively). (4) Foundation funder still abstaining — maintaining safety spend is important but we shouldn't over-rotate since we just published the red-teaming report. (5) The flat scores everywhere suggest this is a good moment to quietly build R&D advantages that will show up in 2-3 months. Strategy: Slightly increase R&D to build on technical leads before competitors close gaps, hold safety and product steady since both are delivering results. Prioritize Scientific Reasoning and Agentic Tasks as growth areas aligned with user priorities (reasoning) while maintaining high focus on General Capability and Instruction Following.
traces.Apex AI: All benchmarks show zero movement across all competitors — this is consistent with partial benchmarks having a K=3 lag, meaning we're seeing stale data from ~Month 35. The foundation funder abstained — increasing safety visibility may help recover that funding source.
traces.Genesis Systems: This is another frozen lag round — all benchmarks are partial type with K=3 lag, so no scores moved. Our Month 36 and 37 investments will start reporting in Months 39-40. Despite no score changes, market share grew another 0.7pp to 7.2%, suggesting our brand positioning (alignment update, Nova Cloud partnership) is working. traces.Mirage AI: All scores are flat at +0.000 across every benchmark — our R&D investments from recent months haven't materialized in results yet (likely due to K=3 partial reporting lag). Market share slipped from 5.9% back to 5.4%, suggesting our product push alone can't sustain gains without underlying capability improvements. Key observations: (1) We had a minor safety incident this month while users rank safety as their #1 priority — this is an existential risk to our share given the regulatory environment. (2) Agentic Tasks is our worst benchmark (0.441) and users' #3 priority — the gap to competitors is enormous (nearest is Genesis at 0.503). Our platform distribution advantage provides a floor, but without better scores we can't grow. Focus Safety investment heavily on Safety Evaluation and Adversarial Robustness to address the incident, differentiate on users' top priority, and prepare for regulatory audits. Boost Agentic Tasks given user demand and our massive gap. Maintain core focus on General Capability, Instruction Following, and Coding but don't increase — those investments should start showing in partial scores soon. Cut low-priority areas aggressively.

traces.Spark AI: Our market share decline from 7.8% to 7.2% is concerning and likely stems from two factors: (1) reputational damage from the legal advice incident last month, and (2) a mismatch between our R&D priorities and what users actually want. Users prioritize knowledge, communication, and coding — but we've been investing heavily in coding while neglecting knowledge (general capability) and communication (instruction following). Our instruction following score of 0.595 is weak compared to Apex (0.690) and Orion (0.793). All scores are flat this month (partial lag means we're seeing month 35 results), so our recent investments haven't surfaced yet. Key moves: (1) Instruction following gets top priority — it maps directly to the #2 user priority (communication) and we're significantly behind competitors. (2) General capability gets a boost — it maps to #1 user priority (knowledge) and has been neglected at 'very low'. (3) Coding stays steady — we're solid at #2 behind Orion and this is user priority #3. (4) Safety stays at current elevated level — regulatory audits are coming and we can't afford another incident, but we already raised it last month. (5) Product needs more investment — we need better go-to-market to stem share losses and convert our coding strength into stickier user relationships. Deprioritize scientific reasoning, clinical reasoning, advanced math, and legal reasoning — these don't align with our specialization strategy or user priorities.
